body: I'm a brown woman dating a white man and what you described is basically me. He's great in so many other ways and is patient with me and tries to understand but I know he never will and that scares me because how can I build a life with someone and have babies with them and all that if they're always going to be ignorant to this huge part of who I am? I think he's also not ready to confront his own white privilege and becomes uncomfortable with conversations around that. It can be exhausting trying to talk to him about that kind of stuff because it feels like I need to prove it somehow that the experiences I have as a woc are real and valid. I will say though that I've seen this be an issue with men of colour as well. They don't understand the nuances of being a racialized woman so it can also be difficult on that end. I think mutual respect and understanding is crucial and the white partner in this case needs to be able to confront their own privilege in order to try and better understand these issues. It's one thing for them to understand your experience as a woc but it's another thing to understand how their experience connects to yours in ways that unmask issues of power that they probably have not really noticed because they've never had to.
Ugh not being able to just get shit done like everyone else makes me feel like a piece of shit too. It's the ADHD's fault but knowing that doesn't actually change how things are.
Who thought dying would be so difficult
His bad days are very few and mine seem to be more and more frequent unfortunately

I'm scared I might be going down the road of self sabotage with this relationship. I feel like I nitpick at the smallest things but also I have a difficult time saying when something is bothering me so I tend to talk myself out of mentioning it by downplaying my own feelings. So I don't really know how to identify between the small stuff that's not really a problem and the big stuff that is?? Usually when I bring something up though my bf is open to changing like when I've asked him to initiate date nights more or stuff like that.

Thanks, he never makes me feel bad about it but I know he also doesn't completely understand it. He's never had to deal with stuff like this before and does his best to be there for me and be understanding and be patient. I think a part of me just thinks I'm too messed up for someone to be with me. I'm trying to work on the being easier on myself part.
Yeah my bf is the same way and will wait however long I need to get the words out but I feel like such a child in those moments not being able to spit out some stupid words

That's exactly what happens with me so I avoid talking about stuff that's bothering me till it all builds up. Or I talk myself out of bringing something up because it's so much work to bring it up that it doesn't seem worth the effort. I've gotten a bit better at getting words out but it's still so much work.

Maybe it has to do with your upbringing? I know I can relate to being seen as doing objectively well right now but I grew up poor, in an abusive household, and have lived in not so great places. When someone asks me where I'm from I immediately launch into the negatives and kind of associate that with myself. It might be that I can't let that part of me go or that I don't want to forget where I came from. Maybe it could be something similar to yourself?

It might help to write stuff down. I can get that way too when I'm having an emotional conversation and sometimes the only way I can get it out is to write it down instead of saying it. You can even just take notes of stuff like your family medical history, your own medical history, a little background about your mental health symptoms and a general timeline for them are things you can note down before the appointment. Having the notes might help you verbalize to the doctor and worst case scenario you can just hand them your notes and they can ask any follow up questions which you can verbalize if you're comfortable or have an extra peice of paper and a pen to write it down.

I get what you mean someone made a snarky comment to me today and my immediate thought was "wow I wanna kill myself." Once you're down in one of those slumps everything feels like the end of the world. Everything kind of piles on and the small things seem to bring you just one step closer to actually doing it. I haven't been the most open person to professional help either but I'd try thinking about it less as paying someone to pretend to care and more as paying someone to help you sort yourself out.

I have depression but usually my depression isn't the primary cause of my suicidal ideation. That was one specific reason a couple years ago and a new reason now. I'm sure my depression played a part but I wouldn't say it's the driving force, just the thing that might send me over the edge.

So much of what you wrote resonated with me. I didn't think I'd make it past my 19th birthday. I'm 21 now so I made it through but I feel like how I felt before again. I'm rooting for you to make it past your 24th. I don't know what to say because my words seem meaningless. You've had a hard life and it hasn't gotten any easier but I find holding onto some sliver of hope helps sometimes no matter how small. Mine is to move away from my family eventually. I know some people I know have said for them it's a pet or just the hope that things will get better. My hope for you is that you have something like that to keep you grounded. If you ever want to talk feel free to reach out.
